newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen opening mixed then pushing higher.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen opening mixed then pushing higher.

text.p: Wall Street shares are expected to open mixed on Tuesday, then edge higher, helped by strength in technology and smaller-capitalization shares and encouraged by gains made on Monday despite declines in the bond market.

An inflation-wary bond market continued to digest recent strong economic data, which has revived concerns about higher rates and boosted yields. But the broader stock market has independent momentum which could drive it, analysts said.
Both markets will also take some direction from economic data due Tuesday, including leading indicators for June.

"The market remains a model for optimism, and expectations remain high," Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co, said. "The bond market is sensitive to the possibility of inflation resurfacing but on balance, the stock market is in a digestive phase where it gives ground grudgingly."
On Monday, the Dow Jones Industrial average ultimately defied a weak bond market to close up four points at 8198. Its rise was led by sectors like retailing and technology.
The Nasdaq composite posted solid gains, rising 11 points to close at a record 1605. Tech stocks were expected to underpin the market again on Tuesday, analysts said.
